title: Pokémon & Monster-Collecting
blurb: The genre that defined the Game Boy Color commercially — Pokémon's second generation, plus the wave of monster-collecting imitators it inspired.

games.title: Pokémon Gold and Silver
games.blurb: The sequel that added a whole new region, a day/night cycle, and breeding, still argued by many longtime fans to be the series' peak.

games.title: Pokémon Crystal
games.blurb: Adds an animated player sprite and a Suicune-chasing storyline to Gold and Silver's Johto, the definitive way to play the generation.

games.title: Pokémon Trading Card Game
games.blurb: An entire card game engine translated faithfully into software, complete with AI duelists modeled after in-game gym leaders.

games.title: Pokémon Pinball
games.blurb: Built on Kirby's Pinball Land's engine, with a built-in Rumble Pak and all 151 original Pokémon to catch mid-flipper-run. Europe's release lagged more than a year behind North America's — the widest gap of any Pokémon title on this list.

games.title: Pokémon Puzzle Challenge
games.blurb: A Panel de Pon-engine puzzler reskinned with Pokémon, sharper and faster than its N64 cousin.

games.title: Dragon Warrior Monsters
games.blurb: Enix's answer to Pokémon, breeding and battling monsters years before “monster tamer” became its own crowded genre.

games.title: Dragon Warrior Monsters 2
games.blurb: Splits into two versions like its inspiration, with a deeper breeding system and a much larger monster roster.

games.title: Hamtaro: Ham-Hams Unite!
games.blurb: The last Game Boy Color game Nintendo ever published, an anime tie-in adventure far more charming than it has any right to be.

games.title: Robopon: Sun Version
games.blurb: A robot-collecting RPG with a battle-and-trade hook nearly identical to Pokémon's, split across Sun and Star versions.

title: Zelda & Nintendo Action-Adventure
blurb: Nintendo's first color Zelda outing anchors a small but essential chapter of first-party handheld adventure design.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Seasons
games.blurb: A dungeon-focused Zelda built around season-shifting puzzles, designed to be played as a linked pair with Oracle of Ages.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: Oracle of Ages
games.blurb: The time-travel half of the linked Oracle duology, leaning harder into puzzle logic than combat.

games.title: Wario Land 3
games.blurb: A structurally strange Wario game with no game-over state, where treasure and time-of-day mechanics reshape levels you've already cleared.

games.title: Kirby Tilt 'n' Tumble
games.blurb: A cartridge with a built-in tilt sensor, years before motion controls were a mainstream pitch.

games.title: Crystalis
games.blurb: A color remake of the beloved 1990 NES action-RPG, brighter and more legible than the original ever could be.

title: Platformers
blurb: From Rare's prolific Nintendo-published run to WayForward's earliest work, the GBC's platforming chapter is stacked with talent that would define handheld games for a decade after.

games.title: Shantae
games.blurb: Released so late in the system's life almost nobody saw it at the time, now considered one of the best-looking games ever squeezed onto the hardware.

games.title: Super Mario Bros. Deluxe
games.blurb: The NES original plus Lost Levels, save states, and new challenge modes, built specifically to show off what color added to a classic.

games.title: Donkey Kong Country
games.blurb: Rare's SNES benchmark compressed into a handheld cart, its pre-rendered look holding up far better than it should on this screen.

games.title: Rayman
games.blurb: The limbless platforming icon's only Game Boy Color outing, built from the ground up rather than ported down.

games.title: Toki Tori
games.blurb: A methodical puzzle-platformer about a chick collecting eggs with a toolkit of one-use gadgets, years before its celebrated Wii revival.

games.title: Mega Man Xtreme
games.blurb: Remixes stages and bosses from the SNES X games into new handheld-sized levels.

games.title: Mega Man Xtreme 2
games.blurb: A sequel pulling from X4 and X5, with tighter pacing than the original Xtreme.

games.title: Bionic Commando: Elite Forces
games.blurb: A grapple-swinging platformer built by Nintendo's own North American studio under license from Capcom.

games.title: Wendy: Every Witch Way
games.blurb: A gravity-flipping platformer starring a teenage witch, an early sign of the studio talent that would later make Shantae.

games.title: Conker's Pocket Tales
games.blurb: A cutesy, family-friendly prequel to the notoriously crude N64 game, unrecognizable in tone from what Conker would become.

games.title: Disney's Tarzan
games.blurb: Digital Eclipse's first wholly original game rather than a port, built in a famously tight three-month turnaround.

title: Sports
blurb: Nintendo's own handheld-companion sports duo headlines a chapter of games built as their own thing, not console ports squeezed down.

games.title: Mario Golf
games.blurb: A companion to the N64 game with its own characters and courses, not a stripped-down port.

games.title: Mario Tennis
games.blurb: Same handheld-companion approach as Mario Golf, deep enough that its RPG-lite training mode became a fan favorite in its own right.

games.title: NBA 3 on 3 featuring Kobe Bryant
games.blurb: A streetball-style three-on-three game built specifically for the handheld rather than downsized from a console original.

games.title: All-Star Baseball 2000
games.blurb: A separately-built handheld entry in Acclaim's baseball series, developed apart from its console namesake.

games.title: NBA Jam 2001
games.blurb: Arcade two-on-two basketball with the series' signature exaggerated dunks, shrunk down without losing its over-the-top energy.

games.title: Pocket Bowling
games.blurb: A GBC launch-window title that keeps ten-pin bowling's rhythm intact despite the tiny screen.

title: Racing
blurb: Five ways to go fast, from a Disney-branded kart racer to a rally sim ported down from PC and PS1.

games.title: V-Rally: Edition '99
games.blurb: A rally racer built around Infogrames' PC/console series, released in Europe as V-Rally: Championship Edition.

games.title: Mickey's Racing Adventure
games.blurb: A kart racer starring Mickey Mouse, built by Rare during their prolific late-90s Nintendo-published handheld run.

games.title: Test Drive: Off-Road 3
games.blurb: A handheld entry in the off-road racing series, developed in-house alongside its PC and PS1 versions. Rebranded entirely for its European release the following spring, as 4x4 World Trophy.

games.title: Xtreme Wheels
games.blurb: A stunt-driving racer with looping, ramp-heavy tracks built for one-more-run replay value.

games.title: Supercross Freestyle
games.blurb: A Europe-only motocross racer that never crossed the Atlantic.

title: Fighting & Action
blurb: Stealth, survival horror, and one very famous case of a handheld game trading on a name that wasn't quite its own.

games.title: Street Fighter Alpha: Warriors' Dreams
games.blurb: A single-player-only conversion of the arcade fighter, without link-cable versus but with the full roster and move sets intact.

games.title: Metal Gear: Ghost Babel
games.blurb: Released in the West simply as “Metal Gear Solid” to trade on the PS1 game's name, this is actually a wholly separate, original stealth game built for the handheld. The Japanese and European cartridges also included a bonus in-game radio broadcast that Konami quietly cut from the North American release.

games.title: Perfect Dark
games.blurb: A top-down action game bearing the N64 shooter's name and characters but built as its own distinct handheld experience.

games.title: Duke Nukem
games.blurb: A side-scrolling action game starring the one-liner-spouting mercenary, trading first-person shooting for run-and-gun platforming.

games.title: Resident Evil Gaiden
games.blurb: An overhead survival-horror hybrid with first-person shooting segments, developed under story input from series creator Shinji Mikami. An unusual release order for the era: Europe actually got it first, months ahead of both Japan and North America.

games.title: Alone in the Dark: The New Nightmare
games.blurb: A from-scratch handheld build of the survival-horror series, developed separately from the console/PC version by the same publisher.

games.title: John Romero's Daikatana
games.blurb: The infamously troubled PC shooter's handheld spinoff plays it as a straightforward action game, and quietly outshines its console namesake's reputation. Europe got the only proper retail release anywhere in the world; Japan's release came a year later only through a Nintendo Power download kiosk, and North America's version was cancelled outright.

title: Puzzle
blurb: Falling blocks, popping bubbles, and one very literal exercise in digging straight down.

games.title: Tetris DX
games.blurb: The GBC launch-window Tetris, adding color-coded pieces and a genuinely useful multiplayer mode.

games.title: Mr. Driller
games.blurb: Dig straight down through color-coded blocks without getting crushed, a perfect one-handed handheld translation of the arcade original.

games.title: Bomberman Quest
games.blurb: An action-RPG spin on Bomberman rather than the usual multiplayer bomb-em-up, closer to a Zelda-style dungeon crawl.

games.title: Pocket Bomberman
games.blurb: A GBC-launch color re-release of a 1997 monochrome Bomberman puzzle-platformer built by the series' own developer.

games.title: Puchi Carat
games.blurb: An obscure falling-jewel puzzler from Taito's deep catalog, rarely mentioned outside dedicated puzzle-genre roundups. A planned North American release was cancelled outright; Europe got it anyway, over a year later in December 2000.

games.title: Bust-A-Move Millennium
games.blurb: A bubble-popping puzzler entry that adds new modes on top of the core Puzzle Bobble formula.

games.title: Hexcite: The Shapes of Victory
games.blurb: A hexagonal tile-matching puzzler developed differently for its Japanese and North American releases.

title: Strategy & Simulation
blurb: An unlikely run of real-time and turn-based strategy experiments, anchored by three generations of a beloved farming sim.

games.title: Warlocked
games.blurb: A real-time strategy game in the Warcraft mold, widely considered proof the genre could actually work on a D-pad.

games.title: Force 21
games.blurb: A modern military RTS ported down from PC, commanding armored units across a simplified but genuine strategy layer.

games.title: Game Boy Wars 2
games.blurb: A Japan-only turn-based wargame in the Famicom Wars lineage, the same design DNA that would become Advance Wars.

games.title: Game Boy Wars 3
games.blurb: A late Japan-only sequel refining the series' turn-based unit combat.

games.title: Worms Armageddon
games.blurb: A from-scratch handheld build of the artillery-combat series, developed separately from Team17's console and PC versions.

games.title: Yu-Gi-Oh! Dark Duel Stories
games.blurb: A card-battle RPG hybrid built around the anime's dueling rules, deep enough to satisfy players who skipped the trading cards entirely. Europe didn't get its own release until a full year later, in 2003.

games.title: Heroes of Might and Magic II
games.blurb: A surprisingly faithful handheld adaptation of the PC turn-based strategy classic.

games.title: Harvest Moon GBC
games.blurb: A distinct, from-scratch color entry in the farming-sim series, not a port of the earlier monochrome Harvest Moon.

games.title: Harvest Moon 2 GBC
games.blurb: Expands the farm-sim formula with new crops, animals, and a bigger town to build relationships in.

games.title: Harvest Moon 3 GBC
games.blurb: The trilogy's close, refining pacing and social systems built up over the two previous entries.

title: Role-Playing Adventures
blurb: Square's absence is filled by Enix, Atlus, and Namco — a deep RPG chapter that leans heavily on Japan-only side stories that never made the trip West.

games.title: Dragon Warrior I & II
games.blurb: Faithful color remakes of the two Famicom games that started the entire JRPG genre in Japan.

games.title: Dragon Warrior III
games.blurb: A remake of the NES-era game many consider the series' best pre-SNES entry, now with a party-swapping class system intact.

games.title: Lufia: The Legend Returns
games.blurb: A prequel built around randomized dungeons and a heavier strategy layer than the SNES originals it follows.

games.title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone
games.blurb: A turn-based RPG adaptation of the first book, wandering Hogwarts and casting spells in a distinctly Final Fantasy-influenced structure. Released the same day in Europe under the book's original title there: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone.

games.title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
games.blurb: A direct sequel expanding the first game's spellcasting and exploration systems.

games.title: Legend of the River King
games.blurb: A fishing RPG that plays it surprisingly straight, with real tackle strategy layered under its cute exterior. Europe waited over a year for its own release, arriving in December 2000.

games.title: Legend of the River King 2
games.blurb: A sequel with multiple playable characters and an expanded fishing-and-story loop.

games.title: Azure Dreams
games.blurb: A roguelike dungeon-crawler with monster-taming and tower-building layered on top, adapted from the PS1 original.

games.title: Revelations: The Demon Slayer
games.blurb: A Western localization of a 1992 Japanese Megami Tensei spin-off, effectively the first color RPG Atlus brought to North America.

games.title: Tales of Phantasia: Narikiri Dungeon
games.blurb: A Japan-only spin-off letting players cosplay as any recruited character, spun off from Namco's original Tales RPG.

games.title: Shin Megami Tensei: Devil Children — Black/Red/White Book
games.blurb: A Japan-only monster-fusion RPG trilogy that predates the Devil Children franchise's later GBA and anime expansion.

games.title: Grandia: Parallel Trippers
games.blurb: A Japan-only side story spun off from the acclaimed PS1 RPG, built as an original handheld adventure rather than a port.

title: Shooters & Arcade Classics
blurb: Arcade history in color — three of Namco and Taito's oldest hits, plus a shooter compilation and two late-system deep cuts.

games.title: R-Type DX
games.blurb: A two-in-one color compilation of R-Type and R-Type II, the definitive way to play either on original hardware.

games.title: Space Invaders
games.blurb: A single-player-only color conversion of the arcade original, stripped of its multiplayer but faithful to the core invasion loop.

games.title: Frogger
games.blurb: A GBC-launch-era conversion of the arcade classic that reintroduced an entire generation to hopping across traffic.

games.title: Ms. Pac-Man: Special Color Edition
games.blurb: A color-enhanced handheld port that keeps the harder, more randomized ghost AI that made the arcade sequel tougher than the original.

games.title: Pac-Man: Special Color Edition
games.blurb: The arcade original in color, maze layout and ghost patterns untouched by four decades of imitators.

games.title: Project S-11
games.blurb: A vertical shooter with smooth scrolling and multiple weapon loadouts, released late and quietly in the system's final year.

games.title: Rampage 2: Universal Tour
games.blurb: Play a giant monster smashing city blocks, with the series' co-op destruction intact even at handheld scale.

title: Licensed & Movie Tie-Ins
blurb: The GBC's shovelware reputation came from somewhere — but a handful of licensed tie-ins here are genuinely well-built, not just cash-grabs.

games.title: Tomb Raider
games.blurb: A top-down reimagining of Lara Croft's exploration-and-puzzle formula, built to work without a 3D camera. Titled simply Tomb Raider in Europe, where North America's box added Starring Lara Croft.

games.title: Rugrats: Totally Angelica
games.blurb: An unusually well-regarded licensed platformer that lets the show's spoiled antagonist headline her own adventure.

games.title: Austin Powers: Oh, Behave! and Welcome to My Underground Lair!
games.blurb: A two-cartridge tie-in split between hero and villain campaigns, published in North America by an unlikely source: Rockstar Games.

games.title: Dragon Ball Z: Legendary Super Warriors
games.blurb: A one-on-one fighter with a huge roster spanning the anime's Saiyan through Buu arcs.

games.title: Action Man: Search for Base X
games.blurb: A toy-line tie-in action-adventure with more genuine level design than most licensed platformers of its era.

games.title: Matchbox: Emergency Patrol
games.blurb: A top-down rescue-vehicle action game built around the toy brand rather than a racing game, despite the name.

games.title: Croc 2
games.blurb: A handheld reimagining of the 3D platformer's sequel, rebuilt from the ground up for two dimensions.

title: Cult Classics & Japan-Only Curios
blurb: The deepest cuts in the whole collection — including a near-unbroken run of games that never left Japan at all.

games.title: Game & Watch Gallery 2
games.blurb: Classic Game & Watch toys reimagined with both their original look and a “modern” reskinned mode, now finally in color.

games.title: Game & Watch Gallery 3
games.blurb: A third helping of remastered Game & Watch classics, including Donkey Kong Jr. and Mario's Cement Factory.

games.title: Quest: Brian's Journey
games.blurb: Known in Japan as Elemental Tale, an overlooked action-RPG about a boy solving elemental puzzles across a fantasy world.

games.title: Bomberman Max: Blue Champion / Red Challenger
games.blurb: A pair of connectable Bomberman versions blending the series' puzzle-action with light RPG progression — titled Hero of Light and Warrior of Darkness in Japan, entirely different names again from their North American release.

games.title: Konami GB Collection Vol. 4
games.blurb: A Japan-and-Europe-only compilation cartridge that finally brought Game Boy Color support to a set of Konami's earlier monochrome classics — never released in North America. The European cut also quietly reshuffled the Japanese lineup and swapped one Japan-specific mascot on the menu for the more internationally familiar Penta from Antarctic Adventure.

games.title: Survival Kids
games.blurb: A desert-island survival game about foraging, crafting, and staying alive with almost no combat at all. Released in Europe several months later under a different name: Stranded Kids.

games.title: Magical Chase GB
games.blurb: A Japan-only port of a beloved 1991 TurboGrafx-16 shooter, a genuine deep-cut for import shoot-em-up collectors.

games.title: Monster Rancher Explorer
games.blurb: An action-puzzle spin-off of Tecmo's monster-raising series, built more like a puzzle-platformer than its console cousins.

games.title: Return of the Ninja
games.blurb: A side-scrolling ninja action game with a heavier emphasis on stealth than most genre peers of its era.

games.title: Koto Battle: Tengai no Moribito
games.blurb: A Japan-only tactical RPG from the developer who would go on to make Mario & Luigi: Superstar Saga.

games.title: Kettō Transformers Beast Wars: Beast Senshi Saikyō Kettei-sen
games.blurb: A Japan-only Transformers fighting game tied to the Beast Wars toy and cartoon line.

games.title: From TV Animation One Piece: Maboroshi no Grand Line Boukenhen!
games.blurb: A Japan-only One Piece adventure game from early in the anime's handheld-game history.

games.title: Daiku no Gen-san: Kachikachi no Tonkachi ga Kachi
games.blurb: A Japan-only spin-off of Irem's carpenter-hero Hammerin' Harry series, built as an action-puzzle game.

games.title: Meitantei Conan: Karakuri Jiin Satsujin Jiken
games.blurb: A Japan-only Detective Conan mystery-adventure, investigating a murder in a trap-filled temple.
